slides.chapter: 1. Get ready and find your way around
slides.title: How Zillow Preferred works
slides.lead: Zillow introduces the customer. You build the relationship.
slides.body:
The program

Zillow Preferred is an invitation-only program, previously called Flex. Zillow connects you with potential buyers. A success fee applies when a transaction covered by your agreement closes. Review that agreement with your team.

Your role

Be available, understand the customer’s request, agree on a useful next step, and keep the record current. The customer may be new to buying and may not know who is calling.

Growth

Your performance and the areas you serve help determine how many leads you receive. Tell the team how many new leads you can handle each month. The limit is 15 per month, or 10 in your first month. You can ask for fewer. The maximum is not a guaranteed number of leads.

Official reference: Zillow Preferred
slides.notes:
Explain the value of a Zillow connection without promising a closing or a fixed number of leads. Preferred and the Premier Agent app are not contradictory names: the app still supports the program. Introduce Day 1 as program readiness plus the working contact record; Days 2–4 deepen conversations, showings, and financing.
Handoff: Next: Before your lead funnel turns on. Connect it to the action you just practiced.
slides.cue: Next: Before your lead funnel turns on. Connect it to the action you just practiced.

slides.chapter: 1. Get ready and find your way around
slides.title: Before your lead funnel turns on
slides.lead: Complete the Zillow setup as well as the TrueHQ training.
slides.body:
Agreement & account

Use your Zillow onboarding invitation and your own account. Complete the Zillow Preferred agent agreement and required onboarding. Ask the team to verify activation; completing this class alone does not activate routing.

ZIP preferences

When you log in for onboarding, set the ZIP preferences available to you. Choose areas you can serve well. Confirm your final routed ZIPs with the team lead; preferences and team routing must agree.

Capacity & availability

Tell the team how many new leads you can handle alongside your existing clients. The maximum is 15 per month, or 10 in your first month as a new hire. Confirm your number and availability before leads begin.

Official reference: Program policies · Agent capacity & routing · Program benefits
slides.notes:
Eric’s activation workflow requires the agent agreement. Show the actual invitation/account path only during a designated setup check, outside the simulated exercises. Zillow’s public routing documentation describes team-managed controls; do not promise every agent an identical edit menu. Academy onboarding requires login and was not independently inspected. Confirm each learner’s agreement, ZIP preferences, monthly capacity, and activation status with the team.
Handoff: Next: The standards you must meet. Connect it to the action you just practiced.
slides.cue: Next: The standards you must meet. Connect it to the action you just practiced.

slides.chapter: 1. Get ready and find your way around
slides.title: The standards you must meet
slides.lead: Know the results we expect, the lead limits, and the tools you must use.
slides.body:
1 in 30

Closing standard

Our team standard is one closing for every 30 leads you take.

25%+

Pickup rate

Answer at least 25% of incoming Zillow connection calls over the last 90 days. Answering 10 of 40 incoming calls is 25%. This measures the calls you answer, not how often buyers answer you.

Monthly lead limits

You can receive up to 15 leads per month. New hires can receive up to 10 in their first month. These are maximums, not guaranteed lead counts.

Follow Up Boss is mandatory

Work your leads in Follow Up Boss. All lead calls and texts must go through Follow Up Boss so the communication is saved on the contact record.

Meet 100% of your assigned Zillow Home Loans pre-approval target over three months. Ask your team lead what your target is. We cover lender introductions and buyer choice on Day 4.

The closing standard and monthly caps above are TRU team rules. Zillow program standards
slides.notes:
Teach the team rule directly: one closing for every 30 leads taken. Keep the 25% minimum pickup rate. The monthly lead cap is 15; new hires have a maximum of 10 in their first month. These caps are limits, not a promise that everyone receives the maximum. Calling and texting through Follow Up Boss are mandatory. Ask agents to report access or calling problems before their leads begin.

slides.lead: We have covered Zillow’s requirements. Next, learn where to go and what to do when a lead arrives.
slides.body:
For this class, keep working in the TrueHQ simulator. These are the steps you will use in your real Follow Up Boss account after training.

Account setup

Confirm the correct team, name, phone and notifications. In your profile menu → My Settings, connect the approved email/calendar account. Confirm FUB calling and mobile access with the team.

People · Inbox

People finds contacts and groups needing outreach. Inbox holds conversations that need your attention. Clicking a contact’s name opens their record.

Tasks · Calendar · Reporting

Tasks tracks work owed; Calendar shows scheduled time; Reporting shows results. Admin settings belong to the team’s setup process. You do not need to configure lead flow during a customer call.

Official reference: Email & calendar setup · Inbox · Tasks
slides.notes:
All class exercises remain in TrueHQ. This page teaches the real login path for the later readiness check. Never ask for passwords on screen. Have each learner verify real account access before activation and observe one search separately; completion here is not proof of live-system navigation. Confirm the team-approved email account and notification setup.

slides.chapter: 2. Update the contact after a conversation
slides.title: The welcome text has already gone out
slides.lead: Read what the customer received before you make your personal contact.
slides.body:
On arrival

TRU sends an automated initial text. Read the contact history to understand the inquiry and prior messages. An automated greeting does not mean you spoke with the buyer.

Your outreach

Use FUB’s calling or texting controls on the record so communication is captured. Introduce yourself, your brokerage and the Zillow request. Invite an appropriate next step; listen before assuming readiness.

After the call

Save the outcome and context, confirm the true stage/timeframe, and create the next task or agreed appointment. Make your calls and send your texts through FUB. If a customer reaches you elsewhere, record what happened and continue the follow-up through FUB.

TRU standard: at least five unique personal calls or texts in the first seven days from arrival. Automated messages and emails do not count; day seven is not a stop rule.

Official reference: Contact record · Action Plans
slides.notes:
The initial automated text is Eric’s team workflow, not a universal Zillow default. Confirm its actual sender, content and trigger before class. Do not invent the exact text or send duplicate greetings. Demonstrate where calls/texts appear in the timeline. Explain the difference between an answered connection, a tour request, and an activity notification. Record the actual result, not the label you hoped to reach.

slides.chapter: 2. Update the contact after a conversation
slides.title: Demo: update the stage after a call
slides.lead: A stage tells the team what has happened with this customer.
slides.body:
Choose the right stage

An unanswered call is Attempted contact. A real conversation with no meeting booked is Spoke with customer. A meeting with an agreed time and place is Appointment set.

Where to change it

On the left side of the contact record, find Stage in the Details panel. Click the current stage, choose the new one, and save it. In our simulator, the green check saves the change.

When to update it

Update the stage after the call, while the outcome is fresh. If an automatic update appears, check that it matches the conversation.

Watch the next screen

Your presenter will show Avery’s record, select Appointment set, and save it. Avery has agreed to Saturday at 11 at the property. A tentative “Saturday might work” would not be enough.
slides.notes:
Explain these three stages. On the next slide, use the shared presentation record to demonstrate the stage menu and save check before opening the activity for agents. Show the saved stage, then invite them to repeat the steps. Shared-screen demonstration does not count as an agent submission.

After an eligible FUB call, Smart Actions may suggest a stage or appointment by text. Review the customer, action, and date before approving. Timeframe changes are automatic. No text does not mean there is no follow-up to do.

slides.chapter: 2. Update the contact after a conversation
slides.title: Check what Smart Actions changed
slides.lead: Compare the suggested update with what the customer actually said.
slides.body:
“Friday could work” is not a confirmed meeting

Jamie says Friday afternoon might work, but needs to check with a partner. No time or property is agreed. A Smart Actions message suggests an appointment for Friday at 3. You also notice the move timeframe changed.

You still owe Jamie a call tomorrow. Inspect the proposed action and the actual conversation. Decide what to accept, decline, or correct, and what work remains yours.

Look for the purple update marker and change log. Check Appointments for duplicates; appointments created by FUB identify that in the description. Keep using the manual record controls when needed.

Official reference: Smart Actions

What to do here

Decline the proposed Friday appointment because Jamie has not confirmed it. Check the automatic timeframe change against the call. Keep tomorrow’s callback task and confirm the meeting with Jamie before booking it.
slides.notes:
Teach this as a worked example. Read the conversation, point out what was not confirmed, and show where the update can be reviewed. Do not request a written answer. Remind agents to use settings rather than replying STOP to FUB notifications.

slides.chapter: 2. Update the contact after a conversation
slides.title: What My Agent means
slides.lead: A Zillow Preferred connection starts a 180-day My Agent relationship.
slides.body:
Where to check

Open the contact → Details → My Agent status. This tells you whether the Zillow relationship is active, waiting for a response, or ending. The contact’s stage tells you where you are in the buying process.

Why it matters

While the relationship is active, Zillow shows you as the customer’s agent and can share their Zillow home-search activity with you. Check the expiration date. The customer can end this connection before the 180 days are up.

How to use it

Use what the customer is exploring to ask a better question and offer useful help. Maintain a real conversation. My Agent does not replace the required buyer or touring agreement.

Official reference: My Agent · Touring agreements
slides.notes:
Differentiate Preferred’s initial180 days from other Premier Agent configurations. FUB needs the Zillow two-way integration. Do not promise all search history, all internet activity, or permanent exclusive lead ownership. Explain the invitation/renewal state and ask the team to troubleshoot a missing relationship. A CRM connected status is not a signed representation contract.
Handoff: Next: See what the buyer is viewing on Zillow. Connect it to the action you just practiced.
slides.cue: Next: See what the buyer is viewing on Zillow. Connect it to the action you just practiced.

slides.chapter: 2. Update the contact after a conversation
slides.title: See what the buyer is viewing on Zillow
slides.lead: On the right side of the contact record, open Zillow Insights.
slides.body:
A change worth asking about

Last Tuesday, Taylor said a three-bedroom home near work mattered most, but had not settled on a budget. Today, eligible Zillow activity shows saved homes in another ZIP and a higher price range.

You have no new reply from Taylor. A partner might be browsing, or the criteria might have changed. You do not know yet.

Look at the date range and the actual saved/viewed homes. Offer a useful comparison and ask whether the search has changed. Treat the price range as browsing context, not approved purchasing power.

Official reference: Zillow Insights

A useful message

“Taylor, last time we spoke you wanted a three-bedroom near work. Are those still your priorities, or would comparing another area be helpful?” Ask about the search without assuming that saved homes establish a budget.
slides.notes:
Explain the right-side Zillow Insights panel and show the original screenshot. Walk through Taylor’s example aloud. There is no written task on this slide.
Handoff: Next: Demo: save a useful contact note. Connect it to the action you just practiced.
slides.cue: Next: Demo: save a useful contact note. Connect it to the action you just practiced.

slides.chapter: 2. Update the contact after a conversation
slides.title: Demo: save a useful contact note
slides.lead: The note should let you or a teammate continue the conversation without starting over.
slides.body:
Read the history first

The center of the record shows previous notes, calls, and texts. Before contacting someone, read the latest entries so you know what has already happened.

What to write

Record the buyer’s request, useful preferences, what you agreed, and what still needs an answer. For Avery: buying with their sister, Olympia or Lacey, three or more bedrooms, and hoping to move before November. You promised two options by Thursday.

Where to save it

Type in the note box at the top of the contact history, then click Create Note. The note should appear in the history below. Text left in the box has not been saved.

Watch, then practice

On the next screen, your presenter will save a note and reopen the history to show it. You will then do the same. A note records the promise; a task reminds you to carry it out.
slides.notes:
Demonstrate Create Note on the next shared slide before opening the agent activity. Show the difference between a draft in the box and a saved entry. Read the example aloud and point out its specific facts. Do not invent budget or financing details.

slides.chapter: 3. Organize and complete the follow-up
slides.title: Demo: schedule the next call
slides.lead: A task tells you what to do and when to do it.
slides.body:
Task or appointment?

Use a task for work you owe, such as calling a buyer or checking parking. Use an appointment for a meeting the customer has agreed to attend at a specific time.

Open Tasks

On the right side of the record, find Tasks and click +. Name the action clearly, choose the responsible agent, and set a due date and time. Save the task.

Make it useful

“Call Avery tomorrow at 9:30 about the Juniper inquiry” is useful. “Follow up” leaves you guessing. If someone else takes over, make sure they have access to the contact and know what to do.

Watch, then practice

Your presenter will create the task on the next screen and show its date in the Tasks panel. Then you will record an unanswered call and schedule another attempt. An unanswered call does not tell you why the buyer missed it.
slides.notes:
On the next shared slide, demonstrate the stage, saved note, and task form in that order. Show the name, assignee, date and time, then save. Open the learner activity only after the demonstration.

slides.chapter: 3. Organize and complete the follow-up
slides.title: Which tool holds which part of the work?
slides.lead: Here is how the tools work together when a teammate covers a showing.
slides.body:
A covering agent needs a usable handoff

Avery agrees to tour 406 Juniper on Saturday at 11. You promised to check parking with the listing agent tomorrow. A teammate will cover the showing and needs access to Avery’s background. Avery’s sister is a co-buyer, not a member of your team. You also received a relevant approved document.

You need to preserve the buyer’s preferences, record the meeting, assign your parking follow-up, and prepare the covering agent. No offer has been accepted.

Official reference: Contact record · Tasks

Note and appointment

Save the buyer’s preferences in a contact note. Put the confirmed Saturday 11 showing in Appointments.

Task and collaborator

Make a dated task for checking parking. Add the covering teammate as a collaborator if they need contact access, and tell them what they are responsible for.

Files and relationships

Store the approved document in Files. Record the sister as a related contact or co-buyer. She is not a team collaborator. Add a Deal when the transaction reaches the team’s agreed point.
slides.notes:
Walk through this example yourself. Point to the matching areas on the contact map if someone needs help. No written response is needed.

slides.chapter: 3. Organize and complete the follow-up
slides.title: Define nurture: two different decisions
slides.lead: Read the history before deciding what should happen next. A later move date and a quiet phone do not tell the whole story.
slides.body:
First, the terms: Nurture usually means staying in touch with someone who may buy later, using a follow-up plan that fits their needs. Your coach will explain when your team uses this stage. Moving a name into a different stage does not, by itself, create a follow-up plan. A task is the dated reminder assigned to the person who will take the next action.

Maya Chen · The move is later, but there is a promise due

How it started: Maya requested a tour through Zillow three weeks ago. You spoke and toured one home together. She is renting until March and said, “I probably won’t move before my lease ends, but I want to understand the neighborhoods before I choose.”

What happened this week: On Tuesday she sent two listings and asked which area would make the commute easier. You agreed to call Friday at 4 p.m. She replied, “Yes, talk then.” She has not asked to stop hearing from you, and no second showing is booked.

What you inherit: The stage is Met with customer. A Friday 4 p.m. call task is assigned to you. A covering agent added, “Six months out — move to Nurture?” You have not discussed how often Maya wants contact or whether she would consider a suitable home sooner.

The decision: It is Friday at 3:45 p.m. Would you change the stage now, keep it while you clarify something, or take another step? What would you ask on the agreed call? Explain how your plan respects her timing and the promise already made.

Jordan Ellis · The record is quiet, but look at the attempts

How it started: Jordan requested information about 18 Cedar Street through Zillow on Monday morning. You called that morning, reached voicemail, and left a message offering to arrange a showing. You have never spoken with Jordan.

What happened this week: An automatic welcome text went out Monday. On Wednesday you personally texted, “I can help arrange a visit to Cedar Street — would Thursday afternoon or Saturday morning work?” There has been no reply. The record shows two property views on Thursday; it does not explain why Jordan viewed them.

What you inherit: It is Friday. The stage is Attempted contact. There is no next task. Another agent wrote, “No response — maybe not serious. Nurture?” The history contains one personal call and one personal text; the automatic message is separate.

The decision: What can you fairly conclude about Jordan’s interest? What would you do before treating this as a longer-term relationship? Choose a next attempt that offers a reason to respond, and explain when you would review the result. You do not know whether Jordan is busy, already helped, or no longer looking.

Ready for a harder question? How would your plan change if Maya asked for one call next month instead of Friday, or Jordan replied, “We bought yesterday”? Identify which new fact changes the action. Do not invent a universal number of days for moving someone to Nurture.
slides.notes:
Give everyone quiet reading time and an independent response before discussion. For beginners, explain lead, stage, task, and automatic versus personal outreach using the facts on screen. Compare two different responses; ask “Which fact led you there?” rather than requiring a corrected answer. Explain the team’s actual nurture rule and why it applies. Do not invent a timeline or imply that a later move date or silence automatically means Nurture. Maya has an agreed call due; ask what the learner would clarify before changing the relationship. Jordan has two personal attempts in the first week, not three: the automatic message does not count. TRU’s first-week floor is at least five unique personal attempts from arrival; calls, including voicemail, and personal texts count. Do not turn that floor into a stop rule or impose a standard beyond week one. For experienced learners, use the changed-fact questions and ask what happens to an existing task if the stage changes. All written responses are ungraded; no rewrite is required to continue.

slides.chapter: 3. Organize and complete the follow-up
slides.title: Repair Avery’s record
slides.lead: You are covering the next call. Decide which parts of this record you can rely on.
slides.body:
A hopeful plan became an appointment label

Yesterday Avery called about 406 and 422 Juniper Lane. Avery said, “Let’s plan on Thursday morning — I’ll confirm once I’ve checked with my sister.” No appointment was booked. You are now covering for the agent who took the call.

The record says Appointment set. The saved note says, “Talked. Interested. Follow up later.” There is no next task. Avery’s interest in the two properties is visible, but the note does not tell the next caller which homes were discussed or what confirmation is still needed.

Before you edit, decide what the record claims, what the buyer actually confirmed, and what another agent needs next. In the following exercise, identify the record’s problems first, then make your changes. Do not create a meeting just to make the label look right.

Before anyone edits, your presenter will point out the stage, the vague note, and the missing task. On the next screen, identify those problems, then use the same stage, note, and task controls you have already practiced.
slides.notes:
Give learners time to read, not just react to a stage label. Beginners can start with “What happened?” and “What still has to happen?” Experienced learners should explain the downstream cost: a teammate could prepare for an unconfirmed appointment or miss the needed call. Preserve the next exercise’s diagnosis step. Discussion has no keyword score; record controls still check saved actions. Demonstrate how to read this record before opening the repair activity. This combines familiar controls; it should not introduce a new workflow.

slides.title: Check the record before moving on
slides.lead: Reopen what you saved.

Stage

Does it match the event, and did the change save?

Note

Does it explain what happened without guessing?

Task

Is the next action scheduled for a real date and time?

Handoff

Could another agent act on this record without asking you to explain it?

The handoff test

You will be unavailable when the next task is due. Your teammate has only this record. Could they identify the buyer’s request, what was actually agreed, and the action they own? If not, name the missing fact rather than adding a more optimistic stage.

slides.chapter: 3. Organize and complete the follow-up
slides.title: Handle a reply from start to finish
slides.lead: Read the conversation in Inbox, open the contact record, and complete or schedule the follow-up.
slides.body:
Read the whole thread

Check My Inbox and the team inboxes assigned to you. Match the person before replying. Unread is a viewing state; opening a message does not complete the customer’s request.

Preserve the outcome

Save important customer context on the contact record. An internal Inbox note stays in the conversation and is not added to the lead profile. A draft has not been sent.

Finish or hand off

Reply, handle the request or assign follow-up with an owner and due date. Close the conversation after handling it. Read status or closing an Inbox item does not update the contact stage.

Official reference: Inbox
slides.notes:
Demonstrate missed calls, texts and emails as conversations. If a customer asks you to stop contacting them, respect the request and follow the team’s communication process; do not solve it by changing a stage alone. Inbox permission is different from contact assignment. Do not let a cleared Inbox stand in for promised tasks.

slides.chapter: 3. Organize and complete the follow-up
slides.title: Use Smart Lists and tasks together
slides.lead: Check replies, due tasks, and today’s appointments. Then work through your contact lists.
slides.body:
Inbox + due work

Handle incoming replies, missed calls and due/overdue commitments. Confirm today’s appointments. A specific promise needs a dated task and an owner.

People → Smart Lists

Saved filters identify contacts by criteria such as stage or last communication. They update as records change. Use the team’s assigned lists; inspect filters if someone is missing.

Read before contacting

Confirm identity, source, owner, last conversation, recent activity and next task. Being absent from a list does not prove follow-up is done; access and filters affect what you see.

Official reference: Smart Lists · Tasks
slides.notes:
New users: explain dynamic list with a concrete example, such as contacts with no recent communication. Experienced users: ask how a stale stage or automation could affect a filter. Avoid building or editing shared lists during class. Missing contact: clear filters, check All People/search, then ask the team about assigned/collaborator/pond access before creating a duplicate.

slides.chapter: 4. Record the accepted offer and check your work
slides.title: What to do after an offer is accepted
slides.lead: Update Follow Up Boss and confirm who handles the Zillow closing paperwork.
slides.body:
In Follow Up Boss

Record the actual stage, accepted-offer details, deal and next task under the team’s process. Keep the transaction coordinator informed about changes.

In Zillow Premier Agent

Final transaction details and closing documents still need the Zillow workflow. A FUB Deal or file alone does not finish Zillow reporting.

Know who owns it

Confirm who logs the transaction, uploads closing documents and handles the success fee. Escalate a pre-existing-relationship or referral question promptly; do not assume it removes an obligation.

Official reference: Program standards · Program policies
slides.notes:
Explain the success fee as a signed-agreement obligation, not a universal flat rate. Zillow’s current compliance page requires closing documents within four calendar days for eligible transactions; the team must name the responsible coordinator and handoff. FUB is the daily CRM, while Zillow remains necessary for this reporting and onboarding. Seller-connection agents need their additional program training; Day 1 does not certify seller-course completion.

slides.chapter: 4. Record the accepted offer and check your work
slides.title: A practical start to your workday
slides.lead: Start with the work that already has a deadline.
slides.body:
Check what needs an answer

Open Inbox for new replies and missed calls. Check today’s appointments so you know when you need to be available.

Keep existing promises

Open Tasks and look for overdue work and calls due soon. If you cannot make a promised call, arrange coverage and leave a clear note.

Work new leads

Read the new inquiry and any automatic messages. Call through FUB, save the outcome, and schedule the next step. Use your team’s Smart Lists to keep working your contacts.
slides.notes:
Present this as a simple daily routine. Discuss how to get help when a new lead and a promised call arrive together. No written response is needed.

slides.lead: Check your accounts and setup with your team. Completing this class does not turn on your leads.
slides.body:
Zillow ready

Agreement and onboarding complete. ZIP preferences reviewed. Monthly lead count and availability confirmed with the team: up to 15 leads, or up to 10 in your first month. Routing activation verified.

FUB ready

Own login works. Calling and texting through FUB work. Notifications and your approved email/calendar are checked. Find a contact, locate its tools, and understand the connected Zillow report.

Work ready

Read the history. Call or text through FUB. Save a clear note, the correct stage, and the next task or appointment. Check automatic updates against what the buyer actually said.
slides.notes:
End the simulated class here. Arrange a separate, coach-observed real-account check before turning on leads; use an approved test contact, not edits to a real buyer. Record unresolved access/setup questions for the team. Do not mark agreement signed, ZIPs saved or activation complete based on this written answer. New saved sessions must use this edition.
